data.gender_notes: Pandiyan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Pandiyan is a Tamil name derived from the word 'pandi' meaning 'lord'. The suffix '-yan' denotes one who possesses or rules over something. Thus, Pandiyan can be interpreted as 'Lord of the Land'. This name is often associated with power, authority, and leadership. The name Pandiyan carries the meaning “Lord of the Land” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Tamil tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Pandiyan usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the land and live with faith, good character and purpose.

In literature, Pandiyan is a title given to the Jallandar Khan in the Silapathikaram, an ancient Tamil epic. The name is also used in modern Tamil Nadu in the titles of local political leaders.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Pandiyan holds spiritual significance as it evokes the idea of a protector and provider. The name is also reminiscent of the Hindu god Shiva, who is often referred to as 'P nerndhana Pandian' meaning 'Lord Shiva, the protector of the land'. This spiritual significance instills a sense of hope, protection, and faith in the name.

It is a name that evokes the spirit of giving and nurturing, inspiring the individual to spread happiness and positivity around them.

historical_references.reference: Pandyan dynasty ruled the southern part of the Indian subcontinent known as the Chera, Chola and Pandya countries, which roughly correspond to the modern-day states of Tamil Nadu and Kerala. The earliest historical records of the Pandyan kings date back to the 3rd century BC.

The Pandyan kingdom reached its peak during the Sangam period (approximately 2nd century BC to 4th century AD), when it was a major cultural and literary center of Tamil civilization. The most famous Pandyan king of this period was Nedumaran, who is said to have ruled from Madurai.
